claude.performance_metric: exited 50% JV interest after ~48 months for ~$4.8bn cash plus retained ~40% Hemlock stake; $2.7bn gain recognized in 2016
claude.rationale: The slice documents that the 50/50 venture was unwound within the outcome window (Corning exited May 31, 2016), with declining equity earnings ($252M in 2014, $281M in 2015, $82M partial 2016) and the CEO characterizing the silicones business as "outside the technologies and manufacturing platforms core to our strategic framework." However, this reflects a strategic-fit exit and financial trajectory only; the slice provides no documented evidence of disruption at the product/process interface (p4) nor of any operations-versus-people/culture fracture (p5). Because the record neither affirms nor rules out these specific interface pathways—it simply does not address integration mechanics—both are coded uncertain rather than 0.

gemini.performance_metric: divested 50% interest for $4.8bn cash and Hemlock stake
gemini.rationale: The slice documents that Corning exited its 50% interest in Dow Corning in 2016, receiving $4.8 billion in cash and a stake in Hemlock Semiconductor. The CEO stated the silicones business was 'outside the technologies and manufacturing platforms core to our strategic framework.' There is no documented evidence of product/process disruption (p4) or process/organization fracture (p5) causing the exit, only a strategic realignment.
